title: Avoiding the Reverse Fall Mistake in Waste Pipes
description: One of the most frequent errors in drainage installation is failing to maintain consistent gravity fall on horizontal waste pipes. When a waste pipe sags or runs level, wastewater slows down, allowing solid debris to settle and accumulate over time. This common mistake inevitably leads to recurring clogs and slow drains. Professional plumbers know that every section of horizontal waste piping must continuously slope downward toward the main drain line following applicable plumbing codes. Always use sturdy, properly spaced hangers and support channels to prevent sagging after the system is filled with water and backfilled.
